final_candidates.decision_summary: G31P has the strongest structure-compatibility penalty among the evaluated candidates and is evolutionarily absent, supporting severe disruption of the compact PsaE fold.
Replacing hydrophobic V24 with charged glutamate is strongly structurally disfavored and evolutionarily unobserved, making it a compelling destabilizing substitution.
V38D combines strong structural incompatibility with evolutionary absence and introduces a charged residue at a hydrophobic position, supporting fold disruption.

stop_reason.detail: The available indirect evidence consistently supports the same three strongest destabilizing candidates.

history.rationale: Introduces a charged residue into a hydrophobic-looking central segment, likely disrupting packing and folding.

V24E is evolutionarily unobserved and has very poor structure-conditioned compatibility, consistent with destabilizing a conserved hydrophobic position. It remains a strong disruption candidate despite the lack of a direct phenotype predictor.

V24E combines a strong structure-compatibility penalty with essentially absent sequence-model plausibility, making it a compelling destabilizing substitution. The charged replacement of a hydrophobic residue is also mechanistically consistent with disruption of the compact subunit.
Proline can strongly disrupt local secondary structure, especially within the structured central region.

I27P is evolutionarily absent and structurally disfavored, so it remains plausible as a fold-disrupting substitution. Its compatibility penalty is less extreme than those of the higher-ranked candidates.

I27P remains a plausible destabilizer because proline is poorly accommodated structurally and has very low PLM plausibility. Its weaker structural penalty than the leading candidates warrants a lower rank.
Replaces a conserved-looking hydrophobic core residue with an acidic side chain, creating a strong packing and electrostatic mismatch.
Although I33D is evolutionarily unobserved, ProteinMPNN strongly favors it on the experimental backbone. This conflicts with the destabilization objective, so it is removed from the active pool.

rejection.reason: Although I33D is evolutionarily unobserved, ProteinMPNN strongly favors it on the experimental backbone. This conflicts with the destabilization objective, so it is removed from the active pool.

history.rationale: Aromatic-to-proline substitution may disrupt both hydrophobic packing and backbone geometry in the central fold.

The structural model disfavors Y34P, but proline is observed in 35.7% of homologs, substantially weakening the inference that it will disrupt PsaE folding. It is retained as a secondary candidate rather than a top choice.

Y34P has low sequence-model plausibility and a moderate structural penalty, supporting possible disruption but less strongly than other proline substitutions. The nonzero evolutionary signal modestly argues that this position may tolerate change.
Adds a charged residue at a hydrophobic position in the central structured segment, likely destabilizing the fold.

V38D is absent from the well-covered homolog alignment and is strongly disfavored by ProteinMPNN, indicating an unfavorable substitution at a conserved hydrophobic site. The charge insertion is plausibly disruptive while retaining a full-length protein.

V38D shows a very strong structural incompatibility penalty and negligible PLM plausibility. These independent indirect signals support disruption through introduction of a charged residue at a hydrophobic position.
Replacing glycine with proline may restrict backbone flexibility and perturb the local turn or strand geometry.

G31P is absent among homologs and has the lowest ProteinMPNN compatibility score, strongly suggesting disruption of the fixed native fold. The glycine-to-proline change is also intrinsically likely to constrain local backbone geometry.

G31P has the strongest structure-compatibility penalty among the active candidates, consistent with severe fold disruption. Its extremely low PLM plausibility further supports that the substitution is structurally anomalous, although PLM is only an indirect phenotype signal.
Hydrophobic-to-acidic substitution in the central core-like region is likely to impair internal packing.

The substitution is absent from homologs, but its very high structure-conditioned compatibility argues that it may be accommodated rather than destabilizing. It is rejected for the fold-disruption objective.

rejection.reason: The substitution is absent from homologs, but its very high structure-conditioned compatibility argues that it may be accommodated rather than destabilizing. It is rejected for the fold-disruption objective.

history.rationale: Removes an aromatic packing residue while introducing a backbone-constraining proline near the structured core.

F40P is evolutionarily absent and has strongly reduced structure compatibility, supporting local fold disruption by proline insertion. It ranks just below the leading candidates because the evidence does not directly establish global PsaE unfolding.

F40P remains strongly supported because proline substitution has a substantial structure-compatibility penalty and negligible PLM plausibility. It ranks below the three leading candidates because its structural penalty is somewhat weaker.
Proline near the C-terminal structured region could disrupt terminal secondary structure and destabilize the small domain.

L65P is not observed among homologs and is poorly compatible with the experimental backbone, consistent with destabilization near the C-terminal region. Its lower rank reflects weaker alignment coverage and a potentially more peripheral structural role.

L65P is supported by a meaningful structural incompatibility penalty and extremely low PLM plausibility. Its position near the C-terminus and somewhat lower MSA applicability reduce confidence relative to central-region candidates.
Changing the terminal hydrophobic residue to an acidic residue may perturb C-terminal packing and local stability.
The MSA has poor applicability at the terminal position, and the structural compatibility penalty is only moderate. Evidence is insufficiently strong compared with the central-region candidates.

rejection.reason: The MSA has poor applicability at the terminal position, and the structural compatibility penalty is only moderate. Evidence is insufficiently strong compared with the central-region candidates.
